Chapter 8: Encounters With Wildness
You know, there are moments along the creek when the wildness of the world just sneaks up on you—so close, it honestly takes your breath away. This isn’t the safe, predictable kind of nature you might find in a city park. No, these are flashes of something untamed, something ancient. They’re powerful reminders that, no matter how comfortable or routine our lives get, we’re still part of a world that’s much bigger—and way wilder—than we could ever control.
Picture this: one evening, you’re sitting quietly by the water, your mind wandering. Suddenly, a deer steps out from the trees, sunlight dappling its coat. For a split second, you and the deer are sharing that same little piece of earth. You both notice each other—its ears twitch, its body tenses, and then, almost before you can blink, it slips back into the undergrowth. You’re left sitting there, a little stunned, filled with awe. It’s such a clear reminder that this world is unpredictable, and honestly, that’s what makes it so magical.
And then, there are those times when the wildness is a bit more dramatic. Imagine a sudden storm rolling in, turning the gentle creek into a raging torrent. Branches break, the water rises, and the air is buzzing with energy. It’s impossible to ignore just how powerful nature can be. You can’t tame it, and you definitely can’t reason with it. Watching it all unfold, you might feel small—but also strangely exhilarated. It’s like the world is showing you its true strength.
Of course, these encounters with wildness aren’t always comfortable. Sometimes they’re downright scary—a snake you spot in the grass, or the eerie howl of a coyote in the middle of the night. But even those moments bring a sense of vitality. They remind you that life isn’t supposed to be totally safe or perfectly predictable. That wildness calls up something deep inside us, something ancient—a real connection to the larger web of life.
Most of us spend our days surrounded by walls, wrapped up in routines that keep the wildness at bay. But for anyone willing to step outside—even just a little—the rewards are huge. Suddenly, the world feels more alive, more real. That creek, with all its shifting moods and untamed edges, becomes a doorway to something deeper—a reality that’s bigger and more vibrant than anything we could ever create for ourselves.
